the Great Basin lakes have existed for a very long time.

the Great Basin lakes are much older than has previously been thought.
the Great Salt Lake has been a large, closed, saline lake for at least 73,000, probably for 100,000, years, and that it is not a recent formation.
the lakes have not lost more than a minor portion of their salts since the end of a major desiccation period ~ 73, 000 years ago.

the salt accumulation times for these lakes are much longer than previously believed.
the accumulation times of salts in the Great Salt Basin lakes are much longer than has been assumed in previous work, and the lakes are probably much older than previously thought.
